No drain-format Powell video exists yet: I tried 13 phrasings, including 'we drained lake powell', 'lake powell drained 3d', 'what if we drained lake powell' and 'lake powell drain simulation'. If we use their title wording, we land as a late clone.

Weak middle and a payoff viewers have seen. The top ~180 ft of the drain is what millions have already watched: Shorts at 5.5M, 4.9M and 4.7M, Desert Rat at 3.4M, 1.78M and 1.22M, and Topo Traveler's 'submerged for 62 years' at 515K. The spine's middle (CH4: record low, Hite, Cathedral in the Desert) is the most-filmed material on the subject. The bottom is mud, not shipwrecks, and the sediment twist plays out over centuries. As written, the payoff ('a dam in front of a canyon it can no longer fill') lands as a quiet 'huh' for exactly the feed we would be recommended in.

The 1983 cold open and the 'too much in 1983, too little in 2026' bookend are already claimed:
- 'Why Glen Canyon Dam started spitting boulders...' Short, 1.5M.
- '1983: The Other Lake Powell Crisis' Short, 45K.
- 'Glen Canyon Dam Tore Itself Apart' 38K and 'The Tunnel Was Breaking Apart' 30K, plus about 5 more Shorts.
- The Hydraulic Record, 171K (3 months).
- Jeffe Aronson, 238K.
- US Weather Alert, 'The Day Glen Canyon Dam Nearly Tore Itself Apart, 1983 Is Repeating'.

The news has turned around. Reclamation's daily data shows the lake at 3,538.11 ft on Nov 6, 2026. That is +21.5 ft above the Sept 15 low, and it is still rising about 1 ft a day. The feed is now all 'RISING'. The premise's 'jumped 12-16 ft in October' is already out of date and will be wrong again by publish day. 'Nearly ran dry' reads as old news unless it is date-stamped and framed so it does not depend on the current headlines.

Phone readability. Lake Powell is a 186-mile ribbon of narrow canyons, so at regional or whole-lake zoom the water is a hairline on a phone. A 100-ft drop in a vertical-walled canyon shows mostly a sliding bathtub ring, not new land. The film's markers (3,516.62 vs 3,490 vs 3,370 ft) are small differences on a large base and impossible to read or remember on a 6-inch screen. That is the same failure as ep01, where mobile viewers left at 14%.

Five premise claims are wrong or overstated as written:
- The record low is 3,516.62 ft on Sept 15, 2026, not 3,519.91 ft.
- Hite was not stranded by the 2026 low (unverified this session: per the earlier fact-check it has been out of water for about 20 years).
- '1983 nearly broke the dam' overstates it. The spillway tunnels were damaged, not the dam body, and the lake peaked 6.6 ft below the crest.
- 'The lake is filling from the bottom' is wrong. USGS says it 'fills laterally, from the deltas toward Glen Canyon Dam'.
- 'Mud creeping toward the dam' needs its scale stated: USGS's first-order estimate is about 750 years to fill the remaining volume.
Any of these in narration invites a correction comment and undermines the 'true story' brand.

The protagonist as pitched is a dam. The 1983 operators go unnamed and there is a two-name cap. That leaves T4 (a human protagonist) failing for a 12-16 minute film, unless the drain ladder is rebuilt around real people at real elevations.

Not kill shots: advertiser risk is low. There is no gore and no conspiracy, and water politics can be left out. The two sensitivities are pinpointing archaeological sites and how Rainbow Bridge is handled, since it is sacred to the Navajo. True material is plentiful, so a 12-16 minute runtime needs no padding.

- The previous record was 3,519.92 ft on 2023-04-13.
- It was first broken on 2026-08-15 at 3,519.91 ft.
- The all-time post-filling low is 3,516.62 ft on 2026-09-15.
- The lake stayed below the 2023 record for 62 days (Aug 15 to Oct 15).
- NASA Earth Observatory confirms 3,517.24 ft on Sept 10, 2026, with a Landsat 8 pair dated Sept 1, 2017 and Sept 10, 2026.

'Within about 30 ft of losing power' is TRUE. At its low the lake was 26.6 ft above the 3,490-ft minimum power pool (NASA EO and Grand Canyon Trust). Dead pool is 3,370 ft: below it 'water can no longer move through the dam' (Grand Canyon Trust). Between 3,490 and 3,370 ft, only the four river outlet tubes release water, at about half the power plant's capacity. The low was 183 ft below full pool (3,700 ft).

The October 2026 jump is TRUE, but it keeps growing:
- +13.8 ft from Sept 30 to Oct 31 (3,518.08 to 3,531.90).
- +21.5 ft from the low by Nov 6 (3,538.11), still rising at 1.0-1.4 ft a day on Nov 2-6.
- KJZZ (Nov 4): about 14 ft, about 26% full, about 5 good winters to reach half full.
- NEW, STRONGER FACT: on Oct 22, 2026 the lake rose 1.83 ft in one day. In the daily record that is the largest one-day rise since June 1964, during the initial filling. The previous high mark after filling was 1.77 ft on June 27, 1965.
- Caveat: a low lake has a smaller surface, so the same inflow raises it more. Say that on screen. The 'biggest since 1964' line is defensible only for the one-day rise.

1983 is TRUE as softened, per ASDSO damfailures.org, Wikipedia and the AZCentral 2019 reprint:
- The left spillway began releasing June 2.
- June 6 brought rumbling and ejected material; concrete was missing at the tunnel elbow.
- Crews added 4-ft plywood flashboards, then 8-ft steel boards in early July.
- Reclamation daily data puts the peak at 3,708.34 ft on July 14, 1983, 6.6 ft below the crest. (Wikipedia says July 15; this data says July 14.)
- The crater was 32 ft deep, 40 ft wide and 180 ft long, and repairs took more than 3,000 cubic yards of concrete.
- The water was 'tinged red from the bedrock sandstone', with 'chunks of concrete the size of office chairs' (AZCentral).
- Electrician Art Grosch: 'We were sitting on a pretty good catastrophe waiting to happen.'
- No damage to the dam body is reported. The cited PopSci link is dead, so it cannot be the source.
- Grosch's 'rising a foot a day' is a quote, not data: the daily maximum in 1983 was 0.85 ft, on June 1.

Sediment is TRUE, from USGS SIR 2022-5017 (PDF downloaded and read):
- 1,833,000 acre-ft, or 6.79% of capacity, lost from 1963 to 2018, about 33,270 acre-ft a year.
- 'Remaining volume ... filled in approximately 750 years', but 'fills laterally, from the deltas toward Glen Canyon Dam, and would likely cease to be useful sooner'.
- Below dead pool, 13.35% of the capacity is already lost, and about 1.73M acre-ft (6.88%) remains trapped below the outlets.
- NPS: about 150 ft of sediment near Hite.
- The lost volume, about 2.26 cubic km, would bury Manhattan (59 sq km) about 125 ft deep. That number is phone-friendly.

The data gap for the twist is RESOLVED. A public pre-dam DEM exists: USGS Root, Hynek, DiViesti and Gushue 2019, 'Digital Elevation Model of Glen Canyon Prior to the Flooding of Lake Powell', DOI 10.5066/P9368XHU.
- 2-m resolution, a 919 MB GeoTIFF on ScienceBase.
- Built from Reclamation surveys: the Colorado arm in 1958-59 at a 10-ft contour interval (dam to Cataract Canyon), and the San Juan arm in 1947 at 20 ft.
- So the true riverbed and the mud thickness can be shown by differencing it against the 2017-18 1-m topobathymetric DEM (CC0). Vertical error is at least the 10-20 ft contour interval.

Drowned human landmarks are REAL and sit at real elevations, which gives the drain a human ladder:
- Crossing of the Fathers: the Domínguez-Escalante ford of 1776, at about 3,180 ft, in Padre Bay, River Mile 39.9. Wikipedia says 'nearly 400 ft' of water, which conflicts with 3,700 minus 3,180 = 520 ft; resolve it from the DEM.
- Hole-in-the-Rock, 1879: settlers enlarged a crevice in a roughly 1,000-ft cliff to lower wagons. The trail below the Hole and the Register Rocks are now under the lake.
- Robert Brewster Stanton's Hoskaninni gold dredge, 1898-1901, at River Mile 121.5: 'a complete failure'.
- 250 archaeological sites were found in the 1958-60 surveys.
- Powell's 1869 expedition named Glen Canyon. The Howlands and Dunn left on Aug 28, 1869 and were never seen again.

2026 on-the-ground facts are TRUE (KUNC, May 17, 2026):
- Bullfrog Marina was towed about 3 miles toward Halls Crossing starting May 4, 2026.
- The Charles Hall ferry was not running in 2026.
- Cathedral in the Desert is exposed, with charcoal graffiti on its walls.
- NPS plans a $73.4M ramp at Stanton Creek.

thumbnails: RANK 1 (LAUNCH DEFAULT): 'DEAD POOL', THE HALF-DRAINED DAM. Hero image: Glen Canyon Dam's curved upstream face, seen from the lake side, with the water dropped to the 3,370 ft dead-pool line. That leaves the top ~345 ft of concrete bare, about 60% of the visible face. One-second read: a giant pale curved wall with a small, deep turquoise pool far below it, so the lake is gone. No real photo can show the dam this empty (the real low was ~3,516.6 ft), so it cannot be mistaken for the bathtub-ring drone shots that fill the feed. LAYOUT (1280x720): the dam fills the centre 55-60% of the width and ~70% of the height. Navajo-sandstone canyon walls on both sides are saturated orange-red, with the white calcite bathtub ring running down to the waterline. Deep turquoise water fills the bottom ~15%. Crop the sky to a thin warm strip; no navy anywhere. More than 60% of the area should be bright or saturated. TEXT: 2 words on one line, about 23% of the frame height: 'DEAD POOL', white on a black box, with 'DEAD' in signal red. The box sits on the waterline, left of centre. A 10 px white tick runs along the waterline across the dam face; this is the one graphic device. Keep the bottom-right corner clear for the timestamp. OPTIONAL SCALE CUE: one white low-poly houseboat stranded on a slickrock ledge in the lower-left foreground, at least 8% of the frame width and tilted ~8 degrees. Keep it only if it still reads at the 168x94 compact size. ENGINE BUILD: (1) Terrain: the USGS 1-m topobathymetric DEM (DOI 10.5066/P9XX0J1Y), clipped to ~4x3 km around the dam and resampled to 2 m, with 3DEP 10 m beyond. (2) Surface: a NAIP 0.6 m drape above 3,700 ft. Below 3,700 ft, a procedural material: a calcite-white band that fades with depth on steep faces, and sandstone colour by slope, sampled from NAIP. (3) Dam: a parametric arch mesh (crest 3,715 ft, ~1,560 ft crest length, 710 ft structural height; check against Reclamation drawings) with a concrete PBR material. The penstock-intake structures stand out dry on the face, which signals 'no power'. (4) Water: a plane at 3,370 ft with a turquoise absorption shader and a light ripple normal map. (5) Light: the upstream face looks up-lake (roughly northeast), so use a morning-sun key light that front-lights the face and does not leave it in shadow. (6) Camera: ~900 m up-lake, ~45 ft above the crest, pitch about -12 degrees, 35 mm equivalent. FRAME 1 of the film is this exact composition with a 2% push-in and moving ripples. WHY RANK 1: the dam is the icon that every host in the cluster (Desert Rat, Eric Hanson, OverBuilt, KSL) has taught viewers to recognise. The text adds the stakes that the launch title does not state.

RANK 2 (A/B #2): 'STILL THERE', BEFORE/AFTER SPLIT. Hero image: the dam and the first ~1.5 miles of the lake, from a high oblique on the downstream side looking up-lake over the crest. The pale dam arc fills the lower third, at about 40% of the width. One clean diagonal wipe, a 10 px white line from top-right to lower-left, is the one graphic device. LEFT SIDE: the same view at full pool, with flat bright turquoise water up to the canyon rims and 2-3 white houseboats. RIGHT SIDE: the same view drained to the 2017-18 lakebed, with sheer red side canyons, the white ring at the old waterline, and a thin dark-turquoise thread at the bottom. This format is proven in this exact cluster ('Lake Powell Before vs After' Shorts at 5.5M and 4.9M), but no long-form video shows the full drain. TEXT: 2 words on one line, about 22% of the height: 'STILL THERE', white on a black box with 'STILL' in red, set on the drained side. The words add emotion (the canyon survived under the water) and do not repeat the title. ENGINE BUILD: the same DEM and material pipeline as rank 1. Render the frame twice from one locked camera, once with the water plane at 3,700 ft and once with it hidden, and composite them along the diagonal in Canvas2D. Camera ~600 m above the river, pitch about -40 degrees. Use a high sun, plus an ambient fill so the canyon floors do not go black. Use the same colour grade as rank 1 so the package matches the film (V7). This exact split becomes the CH3 'full pool' hero transition.

RANK 3 (A/B #3): THE GLASS LAKE, NO TEXT. Hero image: the deepest, tightest meander of the drowned main channel within ~10 miles of the dam (pick it in previs from the DEM), at regional oblique: camera ~1.5 km up, pitch about -35 degrees. The full-pool lake surface is drawn as a thin, glossy turquoise slab floating at 3,700 ft. The near ~40% of the slab is cut away with a clean edge, so you see its thickness and, beneath it, red walls plunging hundreds of feet to a narrow dark floor. One-second read: a lid of water with a canyon under it. The whole gap is in the picture, so it carries no words. Turquoise against orange-red gives maximum contrast, and the white ring sits where the slab meets the rock. ENGINE BUILD: the same DEM and material pipeline. The water is a box mesh cut by a three.js clipping plane, at about 0.85 opacity with fresnel, and the cut face is shaded lighter turquoise to show depth. Below 3,700 ft the terrain uses the procedural sandstone-and-ring material. Use an artificial fill light so the canyon bottom stays readable, and only light haze. WHY RANK 3: it looks least like anything in the feed and best shows the engine's look. But the canyon could be any canyon, so recognition rests on the title; it also tests whether text helps at all. In the film it is the CH2 hero shot, 'the canyon nobody knew'.

pack.cold_open:
COLD OPEN, 0:00-0:30. Narrator: Rodney, ~153 wpm, 76 words, about 29.8 s. Spoken words are in quotes; [brackets] are what is on screen.

0:00 [Frame 1 is the rank-1 thumbnail in motion: the dam at dead pool, 2% push-in, rippling turquoise, the 'DEAD POOL' tag on the waterline. This is the only big label for the first 10 s.]
"We drained Lake Powell to dead pool, where its dam stops working."

0:05 [The camera lifts over the crest in a 2.5 s eased move. The dry penstock intakes are visible on the face, then the drained red canyon maze opens up-lake. This is the first hero shot.]
"Its power intakes hang high and dry. The river can't get past."

0:09 [A low, fast flight up the main channel. Side canyons, the white ring and sheer red walls cut past every 2-3 s.]
"All around it, a canyon that drowned before most of us were born."

0:14 [Hard cut to the same dam angle, with the water snapped back to brim-full. One big label: '1983'.]
"But the real lake once had the opposite problem."

0:18 [The lake at the brim, lapping the spillway gates. Low-poly crew silhouettes on the crest, in the same photoreal grade.]
"June 1983. The lake is full, and still rising."

0:21 [Cut-away through the canyon wall: water roaring down the left spillway tunnel.]
"Engineers open a spillway tunnel to let the extra out."

0:25 [The tunnel exit downstream, with a deep boom. Red-brown water sprays out with chunks of concrete and rock; 1.5 s of SFX tail.]
"Days later, it starts coughing up red water, concrete, and rock."

CONTINUES (outside the 30 s, for continuity): 'The spillway is tearing itself apart from the inside.' Then crews bolt plywood, then steel boards, onto the gates. The lake stops within seven feet of the top. 'Seven feet' is the minute's one number. The story then cuts back to the drain ladder.

RULE CHECKS:
- H1: the first line names the subject and the stakes in 12 words.
- Title payoff: the title is paid off on screen and in words by 0:05.
- H3: the thumbnail words 'dead pool' are spoken at 0:02.
- H4: the hero shot lands by 0:05.
- H5: the story starts at a specific moment (June 1983) by 0:18.
- H8: no named people, one date (1983), no spoken numbers, every sentence 14 words or fewer.
- H6: no menu, no hedges.

FACT NOTES:
- Dead pool, 3,370 ft: water can no longer be released past the dam.
- Minimum power pool, 3,490 ft. The penstock intakes are at roughly 3,470 ft, so at dead pool they are about 100 ft above the water. Verify the intake elevation in Reclamation docs before locking.
- The left spillway opened June 2, 1983. On June 6, rumbling began and concrete, rebar and red Navajo sandstone were thrown from the tunnel exit.
- The July 1983 peak was 3,708.34 ft, 6.6 ft below the crest.
- Nothing in the cold open says 'nearly broke the dam' or implies that the real lake has hit dead pool.

finalists.working_title: The Dutch Drained a Sea and Found 400 Ships
finalists.premise: Every other channel pretends to drain a lake. The Netherlands really did it. They dammed and pumped dry most of the Zuiderzee, and farmers ploughing the new seabed kept hitting shipwrecks (more than 400 recorded) and wartime bombers with their crews. A city of over 200,000 people (Almere) now stands on what was open sea within living memory, and in 1945 the sea briefly took one polder back.
finalists.story_spine: COLD OPEN: a plough in a flat green polder, 5 m below sea level and far from any coast, hits black oak. It is the hull of an 18th-century merchant ship. HERO SHOT BY 0:30: the sea lifts off the map in one move, and hulls lie scattered across fields. CH2: the sea as killer. The January 1916 storm flood drowns Marken, and engineer Cornelis Lely's old plan is finally approved (1 named person). CH3: 28 May 1932, the last gap in the 32 km Afsluitdijk closes (CC0 Anefo photos, Ken Burns, 4 s or less). CH4: the pumps start, the seabed appears, and ploughs race archaeologists. Schokland becomes an island in a sea of grass, and Urk wakes up landlocked (in-world gag). CH5: bombers that fell into the lake are still being dug out with their crews (the Lancaster ED603 recovery). TWIST: on 17 April 1945 German troops blow the Wieringermeer dike and the sea takes the whole polder back within days, and the Dutch drain it again. PAYOFF (about 85% in): Almere on the 1960s seabed, and the never-drained Markerwaard where ships still lie. Final line: in one lifetime a sea became a city.
finalists.hero_image: Top-down view of a 300-year-old wooden ship skeleton lying in a bright green Dutch field with a tiny red tractor beside it, and a thin blue line floating high above to mark the old sea surface.
finalists.archetype: The drain-reveal premise done for real (Contour Atlas drains at 165-170K on 1.4K subs; 'Antarctica Without Ice' 1.8M). Active same-subject hosts: NextGen Manufacturing 'How the Netherlands Built a Country Below Sea Level' 2.96M (3 months), Impossible Travel 2.84M (2 months), OBF 2.73M, Practical Engineering 3.45M. Every one takes the engineering or lifestyle angle; per the ideator's probes, none asks what was on the seabed.

finalists.why: It is a real drain, so the hero reveals come straight from the story (sea to land morph, hulls in fields, the 1945 flood and re-drain, the city on the seabed) on flat, phone-friendly geography (T2, T8). Yes, an angle is clearly unclaimed: "Drain the Oceans, but real." Nat Geo's Drain the Oceans franchise (2-32M views per episode) and Contour Atlas only simulate drains. Here a real sea was really pumped dry, and the film works as a dig down through the seabed's layers. No incumbent asks what was on the bottom.

Proposed structure (reverse-chronology dig):
1. Cold open on the US-anchored find. A US government source says that while the Dutch were pumping one of the polders, "a plane with a U.S. star insignia gradually came into view". It was B-24H 42-7638 "Big Banner" of the 44th Bomb Group, shot down on 22 Dec 1943 with one survivor. The bodies of five crew were found in it during the 1970s recovery, and parts are now in the USAF museum in Dayton.
2. The ships: more than 400 wrecks. The anchor is the English "Queen Anne" merchantman, ca. 1700-1720, near Rutten, with still-filled wine bottles, jars of olives and peaches, and two Queen Anne spoons.

4. The 1945 re-flood as the midpoint twist.
5. A modern ticking clock that nobody uses: the dry land that revealed the ships is now destroying them. Drying, soil settling and ploughing are turning wrecks into "ghost ships", and the Queen Anne's wood was pulverised in a heatwave. check.facts_status:
The core story is TRUE and well documented, but several lines in the premise and spine are wrong or overstated and must be fixed.

Verified:
- Zuiderzee Works: Zuiderzee Act of 14 June 1918, based on Lely's 1891 plan. The 32 km Afsluitdijk closed on 28 May 1932 (Wikipedia's table also lists 23 May). Polders drained: Wieringermeer 1930, Noordoostpolder 1942, Eastern Flevoland 1957, Southern Flevoland 1968. Markerwaard abandoned in 1986. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuiderzee_Works
- Shipwrecks: RCE says "over 400 shipwrecks" were studied, the "world's largest 'dry' naval graveyard" (https://mass.cultureelerfgoed.nl/themes/flevoland). Van Popta's database has 450 (NOS 2021, https://nos.nl/nieuwsuur/artikel/2366226-database-van-450-scheepswrakken-het-hele-verhaal-van-de-scheepsramp), with an estimated 3,000-4,000 wrecking disasters over about 700 years. Batavialand counts about 480 sites. Only a handful are identified. "Largest" is the heritage agencies' own claim, not a formal ranking.
- Ploughing and drainage work did expose and damage wrecks: the first ploughing and drain-laying are named in an RUG paper, and NOS says early Noordoostpolder finds came almost weekly. One plough find was reported (search summary of UKrant, page returned 403): farmer Dijkstra, potato field, a three-master carrying wine barrels.
- Queen Anne: https://www.visitflevoland.nl/en/locaties/974838362/shipwreck-of-the-queen-anne and RUG 2018 https://www.rug.nl/about-ug/latest-news/news/archief2018/nieuwsberichten/opgraving-vroeg-18e-eeuws-koopvaardijschip-in-de-noordoostpolder-begonnen?lang=en
- Four drowned villages: https://nltimes.nl/2020/10/26/four-submerged-villages-found-noordoostpolder
- B-24H 42-7638 "Big Banner": USAF museum fact sheet "WWII Relics from the Polders" (https://www.nationalmuseum.af.mil/Visit/Museum-Exhibits/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/196177/wwii-relics-from-the-polders), Flevoland heritage (https://flevolandsgeheugen.nl/id/10890), https://mass.cultureelerfgoed.nl/b-24-liberator-big-banner. The salvage year conflicts: 1975 (Dutch sources) vs a project begun in 1976 (USAF). The sources say the wreck was "seen 1968" (Dutch) or "early 1970s" (USAF), so say "the 1970s". The co-pilot is called Charlie or Charles Taylor.
- ED603: raised from the open IJsselmeer near Kornwerderzand/Workum in Sept 2023 inside a pumped cofferdam. Remains of 3 missing crew were identified and buried in Workum on 9 Oct 2025. Raid: Bochum, night of 12/13 June 1943. https://raf.mod.uk/news/articles/ww2-lancaster-recovered-from-the-sea-bed-after-80-years/ and https://www.gov.uk/government/news/three-members-of-raf-lancaster-crew-buried-in-the-netherlands
- Wieringermeer: dike blown at 00:15 on 17 April 1945 with two charges of about 1,000 kg. The polder was full within 48 hours, about 3.75 m deep. It was declared dry again by the end of 1945 (11 Dec is common; TracesOfWar says July). No flood deaths, though resistance member A.C. de Graaf was shot. The motive is unclear and must not be asserted. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inundation_of_the_Wieringermeer
- 1916 flood, 13-14 Jan: 16 drowned on Marken (HHNK, https://en.hhnk.nl/podcast-stormvloed-1916-110-jaar-geleden). The total is vague: 19 in North Holland plus 32 at sea per Wikipedia, about 51 per Scientias.
- Almere: 229,574 people (CBS, 1 Jan 2025). Its polder was drained in 1968 and the first residents came in 1976. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almere

Errors to fix:
1. "Pumped dry most of the Zuiderzee" is false. The Zuiderzee was about 5,000 km² and the polders are about 1,650 km² (roughly a third, or about half of the water behind the dam). For US viewers: an area bigger than the city of Los Angeles.
2. "In 1945 the sea took the polder back" is wrong: by 1945 it was the freshwater IJsselmeer. Say "the water/the lake".
3. "Urk wakes up landlocked" is FALSE. Urk stopped being an island in 1939-42 but is still a harbour on the IJsselmeer. Schokland is the one that ended up in fields.
4. Wieringermeer was drained in 1930, before the Afsluitdijk closed, so the spine's order "dam closes, then pumps start" is wrong for the first polder.
5. ED603 is not a "drained seabed" find. It came from the remaining lake.
6. The aircraft count is disputed: about 160 crashed in the IJsselmeer area per Flevoland heritage, versus 500+ per an enthusiast group. Do not give a number.
7. "5 m below sea level" for a specific field needs a source; the polders are mostly about 3-5 m below.

ZUIDERZEE WORKS. Wikipedia: the initial body of water was 3,500 km² and 1,650 km² of land was created. Wieringermeer dry 31 Aug 1930, Noordoostpolder 9 Sep 1942, Eastern Flevoland 29 Jun 1957, Southern Flevoland 29 May 1968. Afsluitdijk 32 km, closed 28 May 1932 (the table says 23 May). Markerwaard postponed indefinitely in September 1986. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuiderzee_Works

1916 FLOOD. nl.wikipedia 'Watersnood van 1916': night of 13-14 January 1916. On Marken 'houses washed away, 16 died'. 21 died in North Holland plus 32 in shipwrecks. The flood led to the Zuiderzee Act.

DROWNED VILLAGES. NL Times 26 Oct 2020: Yftinus van Popta (University of Groningen) identified Marcnesse, Nagele, Fenehuysen I and II. Finds date from 1100-1300, and the oldest ships in the area from about 1250-1300. nl.wikipedia adds that old Zuiderzee fishermen said they tore their nets on the remains of Nagele, a nice true detail.

URK and SCHOKLAND. Urk 'ceased to be an island in October 1939' and still has a harbour on the IJsselmeer, so the 'landlocked' gag is FALSE. Schokland's permanent settlement ended in 1859 and it 'ceased to be an island when the Noordoostpolder was reclaimed... in 1942'. It was the first Dutch UNESCO site (1995). Marken was an island until 1957.
ALMERE. Wikipedia: 229,574 inhabitants (CBS 2025). Southern Flevoland was reclaimed from the IJsselmeer 1959-1968, the first house was built in 1976, elevation -3 m.

ED603. gov.uk (10 Oct 2025): shot down over the IJsselmeer after the Bochum raid on the night of 12/13 June 1943. Remains of 3 of the 7 crew were recovered in 2023 and buried at Workum. It came from the open lake, not a polder.

OTHER POLDER AIRCRAFT in MaSS (Flevoland box): Lancaster W4762 (Slingerweg, Zeewolde), B-17 'Crazy Horse' (Zeewolde), Bf 109 G6 (Biddinghuizen), Arado Ar 196 (Zeewolde), Wellington W5375. There are enough polder planes to say 'bombers came up with the land' without giving a disputed total.
fixes: SPINE: reorder it as a dig down through the layers of the seabed, not a 1916-1968 timeline. Cold open, then the 1940s-70s drainage machine finds, then the Queen Anne's sealed cargo, then the B-24 and Taylor's return, then drowned medieval villages, then a 30-second Lely/Afsluitdijk backstory used only as the reason for the drain, then the 1945 re-flood twist, then the ticking clock and the payoff. Keep the engineering under 90 seconds in total. The incumbents' audience already knows it.

COLD OPEN (true version): a machine cutting drain trenches across a brand-new field hits wood and goes straight through a ship. Use NO27 or the 1947 NF86 find, and keep 'plough' out of the narration. Add the NB36 detail: in the 1950s the first round of trenches missed one ship because it lay exactly between two of them, and the next round found it in 1985. Say 'below sea level' or 'about 4 metres below sea level', not '5 m'.

US HOOK and SEALED-CARGO HOOK: present the Queen Anne as the Steamboat Arabia moment ('a ship under a farm field with the wine still in the bottles'). That premise is proven for US viewers: Curiosity Stream 646K, and Sealed Century 292K in 3 weeks. Make B-24 'Big Banner' and co-pilot Charlie Taylor's return 32 years later the emotional peak, with the Dayton museum as the US tie-in. Before using the 'U.S. star insignia came into view' line, get the USAF fact sheet text another way (it returned 403 to me). Do not state the crew size unless it is sourced. Keep remains off screen and describe them in neutral words, which also keeps it advertiser-safe.

PAYOFF: replace the Almere finale. Better: the land that revealed the ships is now destroying them. Use RUG's 'soil compaction and agriculture', NOS's 'completely decayed', and the Queen Anne's wood crumbling to powder in the heat. End on the Queen Anne's ribs reburied in the outline of its hull, and on the never-drained Markermeer, where the rest still lie. Give Almere at most one line: '230,000 people now live on the same seabed.' End the moment that line lands.

TWIST: keep the 1945 Wieringermeer re-flood (00:15, 17 April; full in 48 hours, 3.75 m deep; dry again by the end of 1945; no flood deaths) as a 60-90 s midpoint. Say 'the lake', not 'the sea'. State no motive, or say 'the reason is still unclear'. Tie it to the theme: water can come back in two days.

FACT CORRECTIONS in premise and script: 'pumped dry almost half of the enclosed sea' or 'an area bigger than Los Angeles' (1,650 of 3,500 km²), not 'most'. Wrecks: 'more than 400', never 450+ in narration, never 1,000. Aircraft: give no total. Drop the Urk gag. Use Schokland ('an island now surrounded by fields') instead, and Nagele's net-tearing fishermen. Do not present ED603 as a drained-polder find. If it appears at all, it is the lake that is still giving things up.

HERO IMAGE and THUMBNAIL: drop the top-down view that oversells. Use a 3/4 oblique cut-away: a green field with a tractor on top, and under the soil (x-ray style) a ship hull and a bomber, with a translucent water slab floating at the old sea level above. That is honest (the wrecks are buried) and reads on a phone. Do not compete visually with the incumbents' dike and polder thumbnails, which are all blue and green maps. No map of the Netherlands in the thumbnail.

PACKAGING: sell the find, not the country. Candidate titles: 'They Drained a Sea. The Ships Were Still Down There.' or 'Under These Dutch Farms Lie 400 Shipwrecks'. Avoid 'Dutch engineering' and 'below sea level' in the title. Test against the RCE map video (601K) audience. Put 'Zuiderzee', 'Netherlands documentary' and 'drained' in tags and description only.

PHONE: open zoomed in (Amsterdam pin, then the Zuiderzee), never a full globe. Use at most 3 on-screen labels and big polder fills with years. For the wreck-dot rain, use the about 289 public MaSS points as a density effect, and narrate 'hundreds' over that shot so the dots on screen match the narration. Credit MaSS (CC BY-SA 4.0) in the description.

LICENSING: there are no CC0 Anefo photos of 1932 (Anefo dates from 1945). For the dam, use the engine plus Blaeu maps. Use the CC0 Anefo 1945 Wieringermeer set for the twist. RCE wreck photos and Polygoon film are CC BY-SA: the owner must decide on share-alike before any are used, or the wrecks must be rendered rather than photographed.

SCOPE CONTROL for 12-16 min (about 1,900-2,400 words at 153 wpm): three named anchors (Queen Anne, Big Banner, the Nagele villages) plus one twist (1945). Everything else gets one line or nothing. There is plenty of true material, so the discipline is cutting, not padding.

titles: #1 [50 chars] The Dutch Drained the Sea and Found 400 Shipwrecks || LAUNCH TITLE. 'Dutch' is in the first 2 words. The open deliberately does NOT name a farmer or claim one specific plow find. The Dijkstra potato-field find is attested only through a search summary, and none of the Queen Anne sources I read (Visit Flevoland, RUG 2018) say how it was found. My web-search budget ran out before I could check either further, so a researcher should confirm both before anything more specific goes in the script.
